이득.before: 한 메타분석에서 여러 연구 결과를 모아 계산했습니다. 독립 표본 259건, 효과량 753개를 다뤘습니다. 물질주의가 강할수록 스스로 보고한 행복이 낮았습니다. 가장 널리 쓰는 다차원 척도로 측정한 결과입니다. 상관계수는 r = -0.19(보정 후 ρ = -0.24)입니다. 상관계수는 두 특성이 함께 변하는 정도입니다. '돈 중시'만 재는 척도에서는 관계가 더 약합니다. 상관계수는 r = -0.08에서 -0.11입니다. 측정한 결과에 따라 관계의 강도가 다릅니다. 위험한 건강·소비 행동에서 관계가 가장 강합니다. 자신을 부정적으로 평가할 때도 마찬가지입니다. 상관계수는 r = -0.28에서 -0.44입니다. 삶의 만족과 부정적 정서에서는 관계가 가장 약합니다. 상관계수는 r = -0.13에서 -0.15입니다. 저자는 매개 분석으로 이 관계가 생기는 과정을 살폈습니다. 심리적 욕구가 채워지지 않아 이런 관계가 생길 수 있다고 봅니다. 다른 연구에서는 서로 다른 집단에 조사 2회를 했습니다. 다양한 인구집단의 응답자들이 경험 소비를 더 행복하게 평가했습니다. 전원이 같은 답을 했다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 뒤이은 실험에서도 경험 소비를 떠올린 뒤 기분이 더 좋았습니다. 물건 소비를 떠올린 뒤와 비교한 결과입니다. 한국에서 같은 결과가 나왔는지는 이번 확인에서 알 수 없었습니다.

source_provenance.abstract: Do experiences make people happier than material possessions? In two surveys, respondents from various demographic groups indicated that experiential purchases-those made with the primary intention of acquiring a life experience--made them happier than material purchases. In a follow-up laboratory experiment, participants experienced more positive feelings after pondering an experiential purchase than after pondering a material purchase. In another experiment, participants were more likely to anticipate that experiences would make them happier than material possessions after adopting a temporally distant, versus a temporally proximate, perspective. The discussion focuses on evidence that experiences make people happier because they are more open to positive reinterpretations, are a more meaningful part of one's identity, and contribute more to successful social relationships.

source_provenance.abstract: This meta-analysis investigates the relationship between individuals' materialistic orientation and their personal well-being. Theoretical approaches in psychology agree that prioritizing money and associated aims is negatively associated with individuals' well-being but differ in their implications for whether this is invariably the case. To address these and other questions, we examined 753 effect sizes from 259 independent samples. Materialism was associated with significantly lower well-being for the most widely used, multifaceted measures (materialist values and beliefs, r = -.19, ρ = -.24; relative importance of materialist goals, r = -.16, ρ = -.21), more than for measures assessing emphasis on money alone (rs = -.08 to -.11, ρs = -.09 to -.14). The relationship also depended on type of well-being outcome, with largest effects for risky health and consumer behaviors and for negative self-appraisals (rs = -.28 to -.44, ρs = -.32 to -.53) and weakest effects for life satisfaction and negative affect (rs = -.13 to -.15, ρs = -.17 to -.18). Moderator analyses revealed that the strength of the effect depended on certain demographic factors (gender and age), on value context (study/work environments that support materialistic values and cultures that emphasize affective autonomy), and on cultural economic indicators (economic growth and wealth differentials). Mediation analyses suggested that the negative link may be explained by poor psychological need satisfaction. We discuss implications for the measurement of materialist values and the need for theoretical and empirical advances to explore underlying processes, which likely will require more experimental, longitudinal, and developmental research.
